text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500 Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP. If you need to run more, such as a 12V fridge or an electric cooler, step up to about 1,000 Wh.

## Light weekend camping (about 288 Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 8.3 lb, 300W AC): PowerStationGearLab's top pick for camping. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. [Review and buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286 Wh, 600W AC, expandable to 572 Wh): the same review calls it the best value. [Same review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288 Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty): confirm you're getting the standard model with AC outlets, not the "DC" variant. [Same review](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **BLUETTI Elite 30 V2** (288 Wh, 600W, 4.3 kg, $275.50 with code AFF5OFF): [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2). Dealectric says its solar input maxes out at 28V, so many 100W+ folding panels won't work. TechRadar lists 200W solar input, so check the spec before pairing a panel. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## Best all-round for longer trips (about 1,000 Wh)
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800W, about 16 kg, $474.05 with code AFF5OFF): [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-portable-power-station-for-camping-2026-review-jackery-ecoflow-bluetti-anke). The $499 price is for the station alone, and the $599 option is a bundle with a solar panel.
- **ALLPOWERS P1800** (1,024 Wh, 1,800W, $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26): [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh). It's cheaper but has a shorter 24-month warranty, and the store page contradicts itself on cycle count.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (under $530 on sale): OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It's compact, but its fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Multi-day off-grid
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (2,042 Wh, 39 lbs, under $900 on Amazon): OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (1,536 Wh, IP65 water and dust rating, about 40 lbs, ~$1,079): WIRED's camping pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Caveats
- Reviewers disagree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 and Anker C300 fairly low (52 and 50) in its lab tests, while PowerStationGearLab ranks them highly.
- I only have direct buy links for the Dealectric items, and those are affiliate links, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy. For the other models, the linked reviews have the retailer buttons.
- None of these can fly. They all exceed the airline 100 Wh limit.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
